title: Ghost-batcher conveyor: resumable, ordered bulk streaming for embeddings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need a single, low-latency streaming path for embedding ingestion that can also accept large bulk loads without losing ordering guarantees or producing duplicates when clients retry. Current streaming and batch paths diverge: the streaming API is low-latency but volatile under network hiccups; the batch/async jobs are durable but add latency and operational overhead. This ticket proposes a hybrid "ghost-batcher conveyor": a continuous streaming endpoint that writes an append-only committed conveyor (durable checkpoints) and exposes an async resume API for interrupted uploads. Goals: (1) exactly-once semantics for client-visible commits, (2) preserve per-client ordering when requested, (3) tolerate partial retries without duplication, (4) maintain P50 embed latency <= 200ms for streaming flows, and (5) scale to sustained 50k docs/minute for a dedicated tenant with backpressure and autoscaling signals.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming ingest endpoint /v1/embeds/stream accepts ordered chunks with sequence numbers and an idempotency token; server returns per-chunk ack with conveyor_offset and commit_token
Clients can resume by providing last known conveyor_offset or commit_token; resumed upload observed by server and duplicates are suppressed
Server guarantees per-idempotency-token exactly-once commit semantics within 7-day retention window (compaction allowed after TTL)
Operational metrics: ingest_rate, conveyor_lag, checkpoint_write_latency, duplicate_suppression_rate available in Console dashboard and alerted when duplicate rate > 0.1% or conveyor_lag > 30s
Integration test harness with fault-injection validates resume across TCP drop, partial chunk, and server restart scenarios (>= 95% pass in CI)
Canary rollout: flow enabled for 1% of traffic for two customers with synthetic traffic; no customer-visible regressions in quality or latency
Documentation: API contract, sample SDK usage (Python/Node), and migration guide from current streaming/batch paths available in /docs/embeddings/ghost-batcher.md
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed. Prototyped conveyor append log using LMDB-backed write-ahead file; resume by commit_token (sha256 of segment+seq). Observed ~12ms median append latency in single-threaded test.

2025-02-18: Design review with SRE & Data infra. Decided to use Kafka only for cross-region replication; primary conveyor will be local append-on-disk with periodic durable checkpoints to object storage (S3). This reduces read amplification for small uploads.
2025-02-22: Implemented idempotency table (tenant_id + client_token -> last_commit_offset) with TTL 7 days. Proof-of-concept PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123
2025-02-27: Backpressure flow control added: server returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After when memory-backed conveyor buffer > 60s of expected write throughput. Added metric conveyor_buffer_seconds.

2025-03-02: QA begun. Injected 10% packet loss: resume path still succeeded for 98/100 scenarios; two failure cases found for out-of-order chunk arrival beyond window size. Added out-of-order reordering buffer with max 500ms hold time.
2025-03-04: Preparing canary plan and infra runbook. Drafted migration steps for existing streaming clients to opt-in to ghost-batcher via header X-Ghost-Batcher: enabled
open_questions: What is the canonical idempotency token composition? Current proposal: tenant_id + client_provided_token + upload_session_id -> sha256; need privacy review for storing raw client token.
Retention window trade-off: 7 days minimizes duplicate risk on long outages but increases idempotency table size. Should we support a per-tenant override?
Do we expose per-chunk ordering guarantees as a hard SLA or best-effort (reordering window currently 500ms).
Failure mode: if the conveyor writer crashes between append and durable checkpoint, can we reconcile via compaction job? Need SRE runbook and an automated reconcile job (low-priority).
